info.title: Fat Zebra Partner API
info.summary: Partner-facing API for boarding and managing sub-merchants and their acquirer connections.
info.description:
The Partner API lets you (a Fat Zebra partner) create and manage your own
merchants, board them onto acquirers, and manage the resulting acquirer
connections. You pick an acquirer (your bank relationship); Fat Zebra
decides which processors carry it.

## Base URL

```
https://gateway.pmnts.io/v2/partners
```

All paths below are relative to that base. Sandbox and staging hosts are in
the server list; pick the one for your environment.

## Auth

HTTP Basic. Send your reseller **username** as the Basic username and your
reseller API **token** as the Basic password
(`Authorization: Basic <base64(username:token)>`). Every endpoint requires
it.

## Boarding is synchronous

Boarding a merchant onto an acquirer is synchronous: an acquirer connection
exists only once it is boarded, so it is always live. A board that can't
complete is reported inline as the POST's `422` error response.

## Envelopes

* **Single resource** — returned as the resource itself, no wrapper.
* **List** — `{ "items": [...], "next_cursor": <string|null> }`. A `null`
  `next_cursor` means the last page; otherwise pass its value as
  `starting_after` to fetch the next page. List query params are `limit`
  (default 25, max 100) and `starting_after=<id>`.
* **Error** — `{ "error": { "type", "message", "fields", "request_id" } }`.
  `type` is the coarse class; the specific reason lives in `fields`, keyed by
  a processor-agnostic field name (e.g. `mid`, `tid`, `currencies`) so you
  never read a switch's native field paths. `type` values and statuses:
  `authentication_error` (401), `not_found` (404), `conflict` (409),
  `validation_error` (422 — something the caller can fix, including a
  processor rejecting a field like the MID/TID), `processor_error` (422 —
  an unactionable upstream failure: a processor was unreachable, busy, or
  rejected us for a reason the caller can't fix; retry or escalate,
  `fields` is empty).

Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC. Merchants and partners are addressed by their
`username`. An acquirer connection's `id` is a derived merchant+acquirer
virtual id of the form `<merchant-id>-ACQ-<ACQUIRER-CODE>` (e.g.
`042-ACQ-NAB`) — not a stored id. Wallets and users carry a stable generated
id of the form `<owner-id>-<TYPE>-<random>` (e.g. `042-WAL-9f3k2m8q`).
Acquirers are slug codes (e.g. `nab`, `cba`, `anz`).

Smoke-tests auth and partner resolution. Returns `{ "ok": true }` on
success.

Returns the partner object: id, name, status, environment, branding,
and defaults.

post.summary: Rotate the partner's own API token
post.description:
Rotates the partner's API `token`. No body is expected. The fresh value
is returned once — the previous token stops working immediately, so the
caller must store the response.

get.description:
Returns the partner's dashboard user ids newest-first in the list
envelope. Fetch the full user via `GET /users/{id}`.

post.description:
Creates a dashboard user under the partner. The `password` is
write-only — it is accepted here but never returned on reads.

patch.description:
Updates the user's `name`, `email`, `role` or `password`. The
`password` is write-only — it is accepted here but never returned.

delete.description: Deletes the user. Returns `204` with no content.

post.description: Locks the account so the user can't sign in. No body is expected.
Unlocks the account so the user can sign in again. No body is expected.

get.description:
Returns whether SSO is enforced for the partner, plus how many users
are linked to the IdP versus not.

post.description:
Turns on SSO enforcement for the partner. No body is expected. Returns
`409 conflict` when active users aren't yet linked to the IdP — they'd
be locked out, so link them first.
Turns off SSO enforcement for the partner. No body is expected.

get.summary: List acquirers this partner may board onto
get.description:
Scoped to the partner's allowed set (derived from the processors behind
each acquirer). Returns the list shape; `next_cursor` is always `null`
(the catalogue is small and unpaginated).

Returns the acquirer's `supported_currencies` and `supported_schemes`.

An unknown or non-boardable acquirer code returns `404`.

Returns the partner's merchants newest-first in the list envelope. Each
item is a summary (username only) — fetch the full merchant via
`GET /merchants/{username}`.

post.description:
Creates a merchant. By default (no `acquirers` in the body) the merchant
is identity-only: `status` is `pending`, no processing connection is
attached, and a fresh API token is generated. The merchant can't take
payments until a processing connection is boarded and the merchant is
activated. Pass an `acquirers` array to create and board in one call
(see **Combined create-and-board** below).

The response is `201` with the merchant object and a one-time
`credentials.token`. The token is shown once here and never again on
reads — store it.

`username` may be omitted; one is derived from the trading/business
name. Either way the stored username is prefixed with the partner's
reseller prefix.

A create is rejected with `409 conflict` (`"merchant exists"`) when this
partner already has a merchant with the same ABN, business name and
trading name — a repeated submit of the same business. A shared ABN
alone is allowed: it creates a new merchant.

**Combined create-and-board.** When the body carries an `acquirers`
array, the merchant is created, every named acquirer is boarded, and
the merchant is activated — all in one call. If any acquirer can't be
boarded the whole request fails and nothing is created: no merchant,
no connections. The failure is reported the same way as the standalone
board endpoint:

* `422 validation_error` — something the caller can fix: an unsupported
  currency or card type, a duplicate/missing `merchant_id`, no processor
  supports the acquirer for the requested currencies, or a processor
  rejecting a field (e.g. the MID). `fields` names the offending field.
* `422 processor_error` — an unactionable upstream failure: a processor
  was unreachable, busy, or rejected the board for a reason the caller
  can't fix. `fields` is empty; retry or escalate.
* `404 not_found` — an acquirer is unknown or not available to this
  partner.

**Idempotency and retries.** Boarding is synchronous and recovery is
always the partner re-issuing a call. Safe-retry behaviour is built
into the operations themselves:

* **Identity create** dedupes on the triple `(ABN, business name,
  trading name)` — re-posting the same business returns `409 conflict`
  (`"merchant exists"`) instead of producing a duplicate. A shared
  ABN alone is allowed and creates a new merchant.
* **Combined create-and-board** either creates the merchant and every
  requested connection, or creates nothing. On failure the partner
  re-issues the same request — there is no partial state to clean up.
* **Standalone board** (`POST /merchants/{username}/acquirers`) is
  idempotent per acquirer: re-posting the same `acquirer` against a
  merchant that already has it returns the existing connection
  instead of creating a duplicate. A `processor_error` retry is safe
  for the same reason.

**What to do on each failure**:

* `422 validation_error` → read `fields`, correct the named input
  (currency, MID, card type, etc.), POST again. Idempotency makes a
  corrected retry safe.
* `422 processor_error` → the request itself is fine; the upstream
  processor isn't. Back off and re-post the identical request, or
  escalate if it persists. Don't mutate the payload.
* `409 conflict` on create → the merchant already exists for this
  partner; fetch it with `GET /merchants/{username}` instead of
  re-creating.

201.description:
Created merchant, with a one-time token. An identity-only create
(no `acquirers`) returns a bare `Merchant`. A combined create (with
`acquirers`) returns a `MerchantOnboardingResult` — a slim payload of
the merchant's status, username and token plus a per-acquirer
boarding status list. A `201` means the merchant and every requested
acquirer boarded; a boarding failure rolls the whole create back and
returns the relevant error below.

patch.description:
Updates the merchant's identity/business details. `username`, `status`
and `credentials` are read-only here — use the lifecycle endpoints
(`/activate`, `/suspend`, `/cancel`) to change `status`, and
`/credentials/rotate` to rotate credentials.

put.description:
Routes to the same update action as `PATCH /merchants/{username}`; same
behaviour and contract.

post.description:
Transitions the merchant to `active` so it can transact. No body is
expected. Activating a merchant that has no active acquirer connection
is rejected with `409 conflict` ("merchant has no active processing
connection") — board an acquirer first.
Transitions the merchant to `suspended`. No body is expected.
Transitions the merchant to `closed`. No body is expected.

Rotates the merchant's API `token` and its `signing_secret`. No body is
expected. The fresh values are returned once — the previous token stops
working immediately, so the caller must store the response.

The response is a bare credentials object: `username`, `token`,
`signing_secret`, `rotated_at`.

get.description:
Returns the merchant's acquirer connections newest-first in the list
envelope.

post.summary: Board a merchant onto an acquirer (synchronous)
post.description:
Boards the merchant onto an acquirer synchronously and returns the
resulting connection with `201`. There is no pending state.

You name an `acquirer` (your bank relationship) and the
acquirer-assigned `merchant_id` (MID), plus the
`terminal_id` (TID) when the acquirer needs one. Fat Zebra validates the MID/TID and `currencies`
against its config and boards the merchant onto every processor behind
that acquirer that can carry a requested currency — you never name a
processor. Omit `currencies` to board everything the acquirer supports.

Boarding is idempotent: re-posting the same acquirer returns the
existing connection rather than creating a duplicate.

Failures are reported inline:

* `422 validation_error` — an unsupported currency, a missing
  `merchant_id`, or no
  processor supports the acquirer for the requested currencies. The
  offending fields are listed under `error.fields`.
* `422 processor_error` — an underlying processor board was rejected or
  errored upstream.
* `404 not_found` — the acquirer is unknown or not available to this
  partner.

patch.description:
Patches the mutable fields only: `priority`, `currencies`,
`card_types`. Changing `currencies` / `card_types` re-evaluates which
underlying processors stay active. `card_types` is narrowed to each
processor's routable set, so a PATCH can't enable a scheme the acquirer
can't settle. The `acquirer` and the MID/TID (`merchant_id` /
`terminal_id`) are immutable once the connection exists.

post.description:
Flips `enabled` to `true` across the underlying links. The routing
toggle only — config and MID/TID are untouched. No body is expected.

Flips `enabled` to `false` across the underlying links — turns a boarded
connection off for routing without deleting it. Config and MID/TID are
untouched. No body is expected.

PartnerBasicAuth.description:
HTTP Basic. Send your reseller **username** as the Basic username and
your reseller API **token** as the Basic password. Required on every
endpoint.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size. Defaults to 25, capped at 100.

StartingAfter.name: starting_after
StartingAfter.description: Cursor — the id of the last item from the previous page. Omit for the first page.

ConnId.name: conn_id
ConnId.description: Acquirer-connection id — the derived merchant+acquirer virtual id (e.g. `042-ACQ-NAB`).

Unauthorized.description: Missing or invalid HTTP Basic credentials.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the resource's current state.

error.message: merchant has no active processing connection

ValidationError.description:
The request couldn't be completed. A `validation_error` is something the
caller can fix — a bad payload, a merchant that failed validation, or a
processor rejecting a field (e.g. the MID); the reason is in `fields`,
keyed by a processor-agnostic field name. A `processor_error` is an
unactionable upstream failure (a processor was unreachable, busy, or
errored); `fields` is empty and the caller should retry or escalate.
Raw upstream detail is never surfaced here — only a parsed,
processor-neutral reason.

unsupportedCurrency.summary: A currency the acquirer can't carry

error.message: currency not supported by this acquirer

currencies: NZD is not supported by this acquirer

error.message: missing required connection fields: merchant_id, terminal_id

noSupportingProcessor.summary: No processor can carry the acquirer for the requested currencies

error.message: no processor can carry this acquirer for the requested currencies

acquirer: cannot be boarded for the requested currencies

processorRejectedMid.summary: A processor rejected a field (here, the MID) — caller-fixable

processorUnavailable.summary: A processor is busy/errored — not the caller's to fix

ok.description: Always `true` when the API is reachable and the token is valid.

fields.description: Per-field validation messages. Empty object when not field-specific.

request_id.description: Correlation id for this request, for support and tracing (e.g. `req_a1b2c3`).

items.description: The page of results. Each list endpoint overrides the item type.

next_cursor.description: Id to pass as `starting_after` for the next page; `null` on the last page.

line1.description: First line of the street address (e.g. `1 Market St`).

MerchantCredentialsInline.description:
Credentials embedded on the merchant object. `token` is `null` on reads
and only populated once by create and credential-rotate.

token.description: The live API token (e.g. `tok_live_3b9c1d…`). `null` except on create / rotate.

enabled.description: Whether card surcharging is enabled for the merchant.

name.description: The merchant's legal/registered business name (e.g. `Acme Pty Ltd`).

trading_name.description: The name the merchant trades under (e.g. `Acme Store`).

company_number.description: The merchant's company/business registration number (e.g. an Australian Business Number, `51824753556`).

phone.description: Contact phone number in E.164 format (e.g. `+61730000000`).

three_d_secure_enabled.description: Whether 3-D Secure is enabled for the merchant.

fraud_screening_enabled.description: Whether fraud screening is enabled for the merchant.

network_tokenisation_enabled.description: Whether network tokenisation (Visa VTS / Mastercard MDES) is enabled.

wallets.description: Digital wallets enabled for the merchant.

statement_descriptor.description: Card-acceptor name shown on the cardholder's statement, max 25 chars (e.g. `ACME STORE`).

government_controlled.description: Whether the merchant is a government-controlled entity.

country_code.description: ISO-3166 numeric country code (e.g. `036` for Australia).

customer_support_phone.description: Customer support phone number shown to cardholders (e.g. `+61 7 1234 5678`).

card_acceptor_name.description: Card-acceptor name sent to the card schemes (e.g. `ACME STORE`).

card_acceptor_location.description: Card-acceptor location/city sent to the card schemes (e.g. `BRISBANE`).

timezone.description: IANA timezone identifier the merchant operates in.

merchant_identifier.description: A partner-assigned identifier for the merchant. Distinct from the acquirer-assigned `merchant_id` (MID) — this is a free-form label the partner uses to track the merchant in their own systems.

created_at.description: When the merchant was created — ISO 8601 UTC (e.g. `2026-05-29T04:21:00Z`).

updated_at.description: When the merchant was last updated — ISO 8601 UTC (e.g. `2026-05-29T04:21:00Z`).

MerchantSummary.description:
The slim merchant shape returned in list responses — username only.
Fetch the full `Merchant` via `GET /merchants/{username}`.

MerchantCreateRequest.description:
Creates a merchant.

Required to CREATE: `name` and `mcc` only. `mcc` has NO default — the
merchant's category is never guessed; omitting it is a
`422 validation_error`.

Two modes:

- **Identity-only** (no `acquirers`): creates a `pending` stub with no
  processing. Board acquirers later via
  `POST /merchants/{username}/acquirers`. Returns a bare `Merchant`.
- **Combined create** (with `acquirers`): also boards each listed
  acquirer and activates the merchant if at least one boards. Boarding
  is best-effort — failures don't fail the create; each acquirer's
  outcome is reported in the `MerchantOnboardingResult`. The merchant is
  `active` when ≥1 acquirer boards, else stays `pending`. Either way the
  response is `201` with the token revealed once.

Readiness — "required to create" is not "required to transact". To board
an acquirer the merchant may need extra business details, depending on
how the acquirer is boarded:

The partner always supplies the acquirer-assigned MID on the
connection (TID is optional). Some acquirers also require additional
business details to board — `company_number`, `trading_name` and
`address`. Missing fields surface as a `failed` acquirer entry
(combined create) or a `422` on `POST /merchants/{username}/acquirers`.

mcc.description:
Required. Merchant category code (ISO 18245, 4 digits). No default —
omitting or blanking it returns `422 validation_error`.

trading_name.description:
Optional at create (defaults to `name`). May be required to board
some acquirers.

company_number.description:
The merchant's company/business registration number (e.g. an
Australian Business Number). Optional at create. May be required to
board some acquirers.

industry.description: Optional. Free-text industry descriptor for the merchant.

address.description:
Business address. Optional at create. May be required to board
some acquirers.

statement_descriptor.description: Optional. Card-acceptor name. Defaults to the trading/business name, truncated to 25 chars.

government_controlled.description: Optional. Whether the merchant is government-controlled. Defaults to false.

country_of_origin.description: Optional. ISO-3166 alpha-2 country of origin.

visa_marketplace_identifier.description: Optional. Visa Marketplace Identifier (MPI) for marketplace merchants.

visa_payment_facilitator_indicator.description: Optional. Visa payment facilitator indicator for scheme rules.

mastercard_payment_facilitator_indicator.description: Optional. Mastercard payment facilitator indicator for scheme rules.

bill_payment_provider.description:
Optional. Whether the merchant is a Bill Payment Service Provider
(BPSP). Defaults to false.

aggregator_fields_enabled.description:
Optional. Allow sub-merchant aggregator fields in transaction
requests (requires an aggregator agreement with the acquirer).
Defaults to false.

customer_support_phone.description: Optional. Customer support phone number shown to cardholders.

card_acceptor_name.description:
Optional. Card-acceptor name sent to the card schemes. Defaults to
the statement descriptor / trading name when omitted.

card_acceptor_location.description: Optional. Card-acceptor location (city) sent to the card schemes.

timezone.description: Optional. IANA timezone identifier the merchant operates in.

merchant_identifier.description:
Optional. A partner-assigned identifier for the merchant. Distinct
from the acquirer-assigned `merchant_id` (MID) — this is a free-form
label the partner uses to track the merchant in their own systems.

username.description:
Optional. When omitted, one is derived from the trading/business
name. Either way the stored username is prefixed with the partner's
reseller prefix. Immutable post-creation.

acquirers.description:
Optional. When present, boards the merchant onto each acquirer and
activates it (combined create). If any acquirer can't be boarded
the whole create fails and nothing is created. See the response
`MerchantOnboardingResult`.

MerchantUpdateRequest.description:
Any subset of the create business/identity fields. `username`, `status`
and `credentials` are read-only — use the lifecycle and credential-rotate
endpoints for those. `username` is immutable post-creation.

merchant_identifier.description: Partner-assigned identifier for the merchant. Distinct from the acquirer-assigned `merchant_id` (MID).

AcquirerBoardRequest.description:
One acquirer to board in a combined create — same fields as the body of
`POST /merchants/{username}/acquirers`.

acquirer.description: Acquirer code (e.g. `bnz`). Must be available to the partner.

terminal_id.description:
Acquirer-assigned TID. Optional. If you omit it, Fat Zebra generates
a deterministic 8-character placeholder from the merchant's trading
name (e.g. `ACMEC001`) and uses it across every processor behind
this acquirer. The generated value is returned on subsequent reads,
and once set — supplied or generated — it is immutable.

currencies.description: Optional. Defaults to everything the acquirer supports.

card_types.description:
Optional. Card schemes the connection should accept. Narrowed to
what this acquirer supports — schemes the acquirer can't handle
are dropped rather than rejected. Omit to accept every scheme the
acquirer supports.

card_categories.description: Optional. Card categories the link handles; overrides the link default.

merchant_tier.description: Optional. Merchant tier; used by the EFTPOS Direct acquirer.

mpgs_byo_profile.description: Optional. Marks the MPGS link as bring-your-own profile.

MerchantOnboardingResult.description:
Returned by a combined create (`POST /merchants` with `acquirers`).
A slim status payload — the merchant's status, username and one-time
token, plus a per-acquirer boarding status list. When this result is
returned every requested acquirer boarded (`status: success`); a
boarding failure fails the whole create and returns an error instead.
Read the full merchant via `GET /merchants/{username}` and connections
via `GET /merchants/{username}/acquirers`.

status.description: `active` — every requested acquirer boarded and the merchant was activated.

token.description: The one-time API token, revealed once on create.

acquirers.description: Per-acquirer boarding outcome — one entry per requested acquirer, all `success`.

acquirer.description: The acquirer code from the request (e.g. `nab`).

status.description: Always `success` on this result — a failure fails the whole create instead.

reason.description: Why boarding failed. Not populated on this result.

MerchantCredentials.description:
Returned once by `POST /merchants/{username}/credentials/rotate`. The
full `token` and `signing_secret` are shown here and never again.

signing_secret.description: The newly-generated signing secret — the merchant's paynow/HMAC secret.

rotated_at.description: When the credentials were rotated — ISO 8601 UTC (e.g. `2026-06-02T00:00:00Z`).

AcquirerConnection.description:
The combined state across every acquirer link provisioned for one
acquirer. Boarding is synchronous, so a connection that exists is
always boarded.

terminal_id.description:
The acquirer-assigned TID (e.g. `T0001`), or a Fat Zebra-generated
8-character placeholder (e.g. `ACMEC001`) if none was supplied at
board time. Immutable once set.

schemes.description: Networks the merchant can transact for this acquirer.

three_ds_enabled.description: Whether a boarded processor for this acquirer supports 3DS.

status.description: Routing toggle across the underlying links — disable to turn the connection off without deleting it.

AcquirerConnectionCreateRequest.description:
Board onto an acquirer. Name the `acquirer` and send the acquirer-assigned
`merchant_id` (MID); `terminal_id` (TID) is optional. Fat Zebra validates
the MID/TID and `currencies` against its config and boards the merchant
onto every supporting processor behind the acquirer — you never name a
processor.

terminal_id.description:
The acquirer-assigned TID. Optional. If omitted, Fat Zebra generates
a deterministic 8-character placeholder from the merchant's trading
name (e.g. `ACMEC001`) and uses it across every processor behind
this acquirer. The generated value is returned on subsequent reads,
and once set — supplied or generated — it is immutable.

currencies.description: Optional. Defaults to every currency the acquirer supports.

AcquirerConnectionUpdateRequest.description:
Only `priority`, `currencies` and `card_types` are mutable. Changing
`currencies` / `card_types` re-evaluates which underlying processors
stay active. The `acquirer` and the MID/TID are immutable.

card_types.description:
Narrowed to the acquirer's routable set; schemes the acquirer can't
settle are dropped rather than applied.

Acquirer.description: A catalogue entry describing one acquirer the partner may board onto.

display_name.description: Partner brand name shown to merchants (e.g. `Acme Payments`).

logo_url.description: Absolute URL of the partner logo (e.g. `https://acme.example/logo.png`).

support_phone.description: Support contact phone in E.164 format (e.g. `+61290000000`).

currencies.description: Default currencies for the partner's merchants.

PartnerCredentials.description:
Returned once by `POST /me/credentials/rotate`. The full `token` is
shown here and never again.

rotated_at.description: When the credentials were rotated — ISO 8601 UTC (e.g. `2026-06-02T00:00:00Z`).

SsoState.description: The partner's SSO enforcement state and IdP-link counts.

enforced.description: Whether SSO is enforced for the partner.

users_linked.description: Active users linked to the IdP.

users_unlinked.description: Active users not yet linked to the IdP.

mfa_enabled.description: Whether multi-factor authentication is enabled for the user.

sso_linked.description: Whether the user is linked to the partner's IdP.

last_login_at.description: When the user last logged in — ISO 8601 UTC (e.g. `2026-06-01T09:30:00Z`). `null` if never.

created_at.description: When the user was created — ISO 8601 UTC (e.g. `2026-05-01T00:00:00Z`).

updated_at.description: When the user was last updated — ISO 8601 UTC (e.g. `2026-05-15T00:00:00Z`).

UserSummary.description:
The slim user shape returned in list responses — id only. Fetch the
full `User` via `GET /users/{id}`.

password.description: Accepted on write only; never returned on reads.

UserUpdateRequest.description:
Any subset of the user's `name`, `email`, `role` or `password`. The
`password` is write-only.

password.description: Accepted on write only; never returned on reads.
